topic: the Lucifer of Liège (Le Génie du Mal) -- a devil statue a Belgian bishop banned from his own cathedral in 1844 for looking too seductive, later bought by a king, while its 'toned down' replacement became more famous than the banned original
title: A Belgian Bishop Banned This Cathedral's Devil Statue For Looking Too Good
description: The true story of Le Génie du Mal -- the devil statue a Belgian bishop had removed from his own cathedral in 1844 for being too beautiful, and what happened to it (and its replacement) after. AI-narrated original commentary.

hook_candidates.text: Facts about the devil statue a bishop banned that sound made up.
Why did a Catholic bishop ban his own cathedral's statue of the devil?
The devil statue tourists photograph in this cathedral isn't the one the church actually wanted.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who jokes that old churches were never scandalous, because they want to prove a bishop once banned a devil statue for being too attractive.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a bishop would never actually have banned his own cathedral's devil statue just for looking too good.
closing_comment: Funny enough, the bishop's 'safer' replacement statue is now the one everyone calls beautiful, while the original banned devil quietly sits in a royal museum today.

sources.note: Confirms Guillaume Geefs's 1848 replacement, installed after brother Joseph's 1842 original was removed for its allure.
Confirms the banned original was bought by King William II, later held at Belgium's Royal Museums of Fine Arts.
